title: Specification Disagreement and Forecast-Transfer Discrepancy in Mortgage Credit Risk: Evidence from Behavioural-History Models
content: Credit-risk models are commonly compared using predictive scores, but these scores do not establish whether specification disagreement is large relative to realised forecast-transfer discrepancy. We compare both quantities on the portfolio event-count scale: specification spread is the full forecast range across a declared model set, and transfer discrepancy is the distance of the observed count from that range. Using 250,000 Freddie Mac mortgages and 12.69 million monthly records, an exploratory analysis compares fourteen updated behavioural-history regression specifications and a retained boosting challenger for twelve-month distress prediction under competing payoff. Transfer discrepancy exceeds specification spread at all nine test reporting dates for the regression set, with a median ratio of 2.119. Adding boosting reduces dominance to four dates and the median ratio to 0.304, demonstrating comparison-set sensitivity. Behavioural history provides modest Brier-score improvements, but representation rankings depend on the specification, and substantial distress and payoff miscalibration persists. Under dominance, the smallest remaining count error exceeds the largest forecast change obtainable by switching specifications. The findings support joint assessment of predictive accuracy, calibration transfer, and specification disagreement: agreement among tested models can coexist with materially inaccurate portfolio forecasts.
